releaseScope: Architecture 3.2, step P4a follow-up (one defect, three vectors): a connector refusal must name its cause without quoting a caller-supplied string. Found while staging the P4a readings for commit - the sentinel value was sitting inside a refusal detail in P4a-readback.json. No engine byte, no contract byte, no recipe touched.
changes: check_credentials: a rejected reference is reported by position, length and reason instead of by value, because the rejected string is precisely what a secret looks like when a caller gets it wrong
validate_arguments: the refusal carries the failing rule and the JSON pointer, and no longer forwards the validator message, which quotes the offending instance
the credential provider error stream is withheld and the exit code is the whole report - an error stream is where a helper might print the value while explaining why it could not hand it over
unchanged: every other behaviour: resolution, attestation (snapshot-only, never --tools), the eight-step chain, locks, idempotency, sessions, artifacts, the materialization mechanism itself, and the three published engine-facing shapes
openDeferred: the same quoting habit is worth a look in the recipe-facing refusals that echo a placeholder or a path; those carry no caller secret today, and no change was made there without a test that proves one is needed
D-88 stands: a component release carries no manifest any published schema constrains, so "passes its own schema" remains self-certification until the contract generation takes it
pointerPolicy: software/_connector/current.json moves 1.0.1 -> 1.0.2, same discipline as the 1.0.1 move and carrying the same registered deviation: this resource has no platform config reader yet. 1.0.1 is left in place because it holds a value-echoing refusal.
